To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cartilage strains in mouse knees are highly dependent on the level of muscular force applied and that cartilage deformation recovery is highly dependent on the duration of the applied force and on the level of force applied.
cartilage strains of up to 18% can be measured in the mouse knee in vivo during controlled muscle contractions and that cartilage deformation recovery is highly time dependent.
cartilage and cell strains in mouse knees are highly dependent on muscular loading and that these strains are dynamic, viscoelastic and can be accurately measured.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of articular cartilage strain in the knee of a live, intact mouse.
measuring in vivo, real-time articular cartilage deformation in intact joints of live animals under precisely controlled, dynamic muscular load application.
the measurement of articular cartilage deformation during in vivo, dynamic muscular loading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cartilage of a mouse knee is capable of deforming in a dynamic manner in response to precisely controlled muscular forces.
articular cartilage deformation is a function of the applied force and the duration of the applied force.
the articular cartilages of synovial joints undergo substantial deformation when loaded by controlled muscular contractions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
articular cartilage deformation is substantial during physiological muscular loading and that it is highly viscoelastic.
the cartilage of the mouse knee can be loaded by muscular contractions in a controlled manner and the resulting deformations can be quantified.
the articular cartilege of the knee joint deforms significantly under physiological loads, but that the deformation is reversible and does not lead to permanent structural tissue damage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cartilage deformation can be measured dynamically in vivo and that the deformation response is viscoelastic.
cartilage deformation is highly dependent on the applied load and the loading conditions.
articular cartilage deformation in the knee is highly dependent on the applied load.
